title: Rosetta Stone
idiom: ink rubbing of a carved trilingual stele — one meaning across three notations
hero_prompt: A wide darkened backdrop rendered as an ink rubbing of an ancient carved stone stele — a single tall dark slab fills the center, divided into three stacked horizontal registers. Each register is carved with a different family of abstract marks: the top band angular wedge-cuts, the middle band flowing organic glyphs, the bottom band precise geometric diagram-signs — and faint vertical guide-lines link one mark to its counterpart in the bands above and below, showing a single meaning translated across three notations. Weathered stone texture, chiselled shadow, warm torchlight raking across the relief, upper register darkened. Deliberately not real writing — invented abstract glyphs only. No letters, numerals, words, labels, real inscriptions — purely pictorial.
icon_prompt: Bold high-contrast square emblem: a single upright stone tablet split into three bold horizontal bands, each band holding one large distinct abstract glyph — a wedge, a spiral, a triangle-grid — with a thin vertical line threading through all three to show alignment. Heavy carved outline, stark two-value, no fine linework, survives at 24px. No letters, numerals, words, labels — purely pictorial.
